title: German Intelligence REVEALS Russia's ATTACK on NATO is IMMINENT!
summary: A 2025 explainer reports German intelligence and military warnings that Russia is rebuilding its forces to be able to fight NATO by the end of the decade and is already waging sabotage against Europe.

assertions.quote: Russia might create the conditions for a “large-scale conventional war” against NATO by the end of the decade

verdicts.note: Linked Metaculus forecasts give 55% that Russia attacks a European NATO member before 2035 and a median date of September 2030, consistent with readiness around 2030, though they measure an attack, not readiness.

DDIS's timeline has Russia ready for a local war about six months after the Ukraine war stops or freezes, a regional war within two years and a large-scale war within five, conditional on NATO looking weak and failing to keep pace.

assertions.quote: the imminent attack against NATO could take place virtually anywhere

verdicts.note: Metaculus forecasters put a direct Russia-NATO conflict (troops across a border or a deliberate deadly attack) at 4.2% before 2027; a linked question with only 24 forecasters puts a Russian attack on a European NATO member before 2035 at 55%.
Polymarket priced a Russian offensive to take any part of a NATO country by December 31, 2026 at 4.5%.
FRI's median expert put 500+ militarized deaths between Russia and a NATO country other than the US before 2030 at 10% (superforecasters 5.5%).

Estonia's foreign intelligence (Feb 2026) assesses Russia has no intention of attacking Estonia or any NATO member in the coming year and expects the same next year, while warning capabilities will grow.
Eurasia Group sees the main 2026 danger as Russian hybrid war on NATO (sabotage, airspace probes) and more frequent confrontations, not a military attack on a member.
CFR's experts rate armed clashes between Russia and NATO members at an even chance in 2026, which is clashes from provocations rather than a planned attack.

assertions.quote: Russia is already waging an escalating campaign of subversion and sabotage against European targets

verdicts.note: The Bulletin notes Russian drone incursions into NATO countries heightened European threat perceptions; it does not cover sabotage or establish that the aim is to test NATO.

Danish intelligence assesses Russia is waging hybrid war on NATO with sabotage and cyber attacks, and that its autumn 2025 drone violation of Polish airspace was likely a deliberate provocation to test NATO's responses.

US intelligence cites Russia's continued sabotage against US and European allies, such as the November 2025 railway explosion in Poland, and lists gray-zone tools including sabotage and military intimidation.
Eurasia Group expects Russia to escalate gray-zone operations against NATO in 2026, from infrastructure sabotage to airspace probes and election interference.
The Munich Security Report says Russia is intensifying its hybrid warfare campaign across Europe.

assertions.quote: this plan is almost tailor-made to face the exact threats posed by Russia

verdicts.note: SIPRI attributes Europe's rise to instability from the Russia-Ukraine war and uncertainty over US security guarantees, which supports a Russia-driven rearmament but not that governments expect a war.
DDIS ties European rearmament to the Russian threat and doubts about the US as guarantor, framed as strengthening deterrence rather than expecting a war.

US intelligence says most European countries regard Russia as their greatest adversary and its invasion and gray-zone attacks have galvanised their defence focus; deterrence, not an expected war, is the stated aim.

assertions.quote: In PPP terms, Russia’s military spending is estimated at around $461.6 billion.

verdicts.note: IISS-style PPP estimates put Russia near Europe's nominal total, but that compares a PPP figure with a nominal one; Europe's own PPP spending is higher.

assertions.quote: by 2026, the Russian military plans to boost its ranks to 2.39 million soldiers

verdicts.note: DDIS: troop numbers rose from about one million to nearly 1.5 million since the invasion, and new factories let Russia make drones, cruise and ballistic missiles in far greater quantities than before the war.
US intelligence says Russia's ground forces have grown despite wartime attrition and Russia fields advanced systems including hypersonic missiles.

assertions.quote: the country’s military capabilities have been decimated in Ukraine, suffering record losses

verdicts.note: Western estimates put Russian casualties near a million by 2025, although Ukraine's equipment counts are higher than independently verified losses.
SIPRI mentions drones partly compensating for Russia's earlier losses of costly aircraft and armoured vehicles, which supports equipment losses but gives no scale and says nothing on troops.
RAND (2023) records devastating consequences for Russian forces and accumulating losses that have made Russia more fearful of NATO.
EFIS: in nearly four years Russia has lost around one million soldiers killed or severely injured and exhausted most of its Soviet-era military stockpiles.
UCDP: confirmed Russian battlefield deaths rose every year, from 42,000 in 2022 to 77,700 in 2025, against 14,000-24,000 a year for Ukraine, and these figures are expected to be revised upward.
PRIO: the Russia-Ukraine war caused about 370,000 battle deaths in 2022-2025, the most for any single conflict since 1989 (both sides combined).

assertions.quote: Russia might try to target one or more NATO countries individually

verdicts.note: A claim about Russian intent; Lithuanian and German services warn of it, but no public record shows such a plan.
DDIS expects stronger Russian military provocations, possibly to test whether the US would come to Europe's aid, if Washington cast doubt on its commitment; provocations rather than an attack.
